message.content:
Mitochondria are abundant organelles found in almost all eukaryotic cells. Their number can vary widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands:

| Cell Type (or Organism) | Typical Mitochondrial Count |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Human skeletal muscle fibers** | ~10 000–30 000 per cell (highly energy‑dependent) |
| **Neurons (especially axons)** | ~5 000–20 000 per neuron (energy‑intensive signaling) |
| **Red blood cells (mature human RBCs)** | 0 (they lack mitochondria after maturation) |
| **Typical mammalian somatic cell** | ~200–500 per cell (average estimate) |
| **Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae)** | ~50–150 per cell (depends on growth phase) |
| **Plant leaf mesophyll cells** | ~300–800 per cell (photosynthetic activity) |

These figures are averages; actual counts can differ due to factors such as cell cycle stage, differentiation status, and environmental conditions. If you need a precise count for a specific cell line or organism, specialized imaging techniques like electron microscopy combined with quantitative image analysis would be required.
